liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **The Seven** (5 reviews): Garcia and band sound frantic and serpentine in this jam, playing with great intensity; Reviewer calls it a stunning, unexpected jam, worth top marks by itself [3][7][10][11][12]
- **Doin' That Rag** (1 review): Reviewer describes the opening Doin' That Rag as ill-fated [7]
- **Good Lovin** (1 review): Reviewer finds the Good Lovin' only so-so compared with the rest of the show [11]

## Setlist highlights

- **The Seven**: rare: 4 archived performances [15]

## The recordings

- **gd69-09-29.aud.early.hollister.79.sbeok.shnf** (recommended): audience recording; 7 songs; 43 min; rated 4.05/5 by 19 [1]. Said about its sound: Recording is overwhelmingly bright and dull in response, which the reviewer blames on the cheap cassette; no digital EQ was applied; Sound quality is lacking, but headphones help; Sound is hard going, with vocals washed out in places [8][10][11]
- **gd1969-09-29.176878.early.aud.remaster.mcallister.daniel.flac1644**: audience recording; 5 songs; 43 min; rated 5/5 by 1 [2]. Said about its sound: Original fileset's playback speed varied widely; the remaster improves it, though not perfectly [2]

## Around the show

- Cafe au Go Go was a tiny 400-seat Greenwich Village club, known for Lenny Bruce's obscenity arrests [14]
- Ranks The Seven alongside 5/21/74 PITB, 7/27/73 Jam>Wharf Rat and 12/6/73 DS as surprise jam highlights [7]
- Seven months after Live/Dead was recorded, the band was heading toward Workingman's yet kept its psychedelic power, as this night and the next show [14]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd69-09-29.aud.early.hollister.79.sbeok.shnf**: transferred by Brian McAllister; source: Audience [1]. Also: Reviewer long knew this night from an old cassette, believed to be from the Action House, Long Beach LI; Best available version comes from a Maxell UD cassette, a tape type meant for voice dictation; Early-show audience recording passed through reel and Maxell UD Dolby B cassette, then DAT, ZA2 and DiamondCut noise reduction to CD [1][6][8]
- **gd1969-09-29.176878.early.aud.remaster.mcallister.daniel.flac1644**: source: AUD > reel master > ? > Cassette (Maxell UD / Dolby B) [2]. Also: Remaster of the earlier shn 79 fileset, using a source supplied by Brian McAllister [2]
